contents.name: Section 2.5.1 Basic Properties (printed pp. 96-98)
contents.support: The equilibrium interior field E = 0, the constant potential, the surface location of the charge and the equipotential surface are the conductor model's clauses.

contents.name: Section 2.5.2 Induced Charges (printed pp. 98-102)
contents.reason: The induced-charge examples and the empty-cavity shielding discussion are not part of this pair's reserved inventory, and the model formulated here assumes a connected vacuum region; cavity configurations would need their own page-level treatment.

contents.name: Section 2.5.3 Surface charge and the force on a conductor, Eqs. (2.48)-(2.49) (printed pp. 102-103)
contents.support: The normal field sigma/epsilon_0 just outside and the normal-derivative form sigma = -epsilon_0 dV/dn are proved pointwise in the item under its one-sided regularity hypothesis.

contents.name: Section 2.5.3 mechanical force per unit area f = sigma E_average, Eq. (2.50) (printed p. 103)
contents.reason: Conductor surface forces are not promised by this pair's reserved inventory (no force item on the A or B page); the passage is recorded for source fidelity and deliberately not built.

contents.name: Section 2.5.4 Capacitors, C = Q/V and Example 2.10 parallel plate (printed pp. 103-105)
contents.support: C = Q/V, its geometric dependence, positivity and the charging energy Q^2/2C are the theorem's conclusions; Example 2.10 supports the ideal parallel-plate computation.

contents.name: Example 2.11 concentric spherical shells (printed p. 105)
contents.reason: The concentric-sphere capacitor is not in the pair's reserved B inventory (grounded-plane force, parallel plates, Neumann failure); the passage is recorded but not built.

contents.name: Sections 3.1.5-3.1.6 Uniqueness theorems (printed pp. 116-121)
contents.support: The first and second uniqueness theorems are the classical backbone of the Dirichlet/Neumann uniqueness clauses; the cavity corollary is outside the connected-vacuum scope.

contents.name: Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2 The classic image problem and induced surface charge, Eqs. (3.9)-(3.11) (printed pp. 121-123)
contents.support: The candidate image potential, its zero plane trace, the induced density (3.10) and the total induced charge -q (3.11) are the certificate's content.

contents.name: Section 3.2.3 Force, Eq. (3.12) (printed p. 123)
contents.support: The image-pair force computation supplies the magnitude q^2/(16 pi epsilon_0 a^2) and its attraction direction.

contents.name: Section 3.2.3 Energy, Eqs. (3.13)-(3.14) (printed pp. 123-124)
contents.reason: The image-pair and single-charge image energies are not part of the pair's reserved inventory; only the force (3.12) is built as the B example.

contents.name: Section 2.4 Conductors and Eq. (2.31) (printed pp. 30-31)
